content.key_idea: A traditional DCN distributes clock via a static spanning tree of electrical switches, whereas an RDCN's optical circuit switches reconfigure dynamic circuits between endpoints over time.
content.reading_order: Left to right across the three panels: static tree (a), reconfigurable endpoint-OCS topology (b), then the OCS's internal time-varying configuration (c).

summary: Figure 1 contrasts a traditional data center network with a reconfigurable one (RDCN) to motivate SyncWise. Panel (a) shows a traditional DCN as a static tree of electrical switches connecting communication endpoints, with clock propagation following the tree edges, matching how protocols like PTP operate. Panel (b) shows an RDCN where endpoints instead connect through optical circuit switches (OCSes, two shown), which establish dynamic optical circuits between endpoint pairs rather than fixed cabling. Panel (c), 'OCS Configuration,' schematically depicts the OCS's internal switching fabric changing its endpoint-to-endpoint connections over time. Together the three panels argue that an RDCN's dynamically changing topology invalidates static, tree-based clock-propagation schemes, motivating SyncWise's error-aware synchronization design. A legend spanning the top of the figure defines the switch, endpoint, cable, OCS and clock-propagation symbols shared by all three panels.
summary_zh: 该图对比传统数据中心网络与可重构网络(RDCN)：(a)电交换机构成生成树、时钟沿树传播；(b)端点经光交换机(OCS)建立动态光路；(c)展示 OCS 内部连接随时间重构，说明静态同步方案为何失效。
